patch_description:
The current candidate (plain RY-RZ-CZ-RY-RZ ansatz) scores only 0.83, clearly worse than the modular, skip-connected, shared-parameter architecture that previously achieved 0.89 combined score with better generalization gap and loss. I restore that stronger modular architecture (per-qubit RY, ring CRZ, per-qubit RX, skip-2/skip-3/diameter CRZ entanglers, block repeated twice with shared params) and additionally insert the recommended mirror-paired RZ phase layer between the RX layer and the skip-2 entangler. The mirror RZ layer applies RZ to antipodal-ish pairs (0&7, 1&6, 2&5, 3&4) sharing 4 parameters, adding symmetric local phase control that should sharpen expressivity and help convergence without inflating parameter count much (+4 params per block usage, but since params are shared by name across both block copies, total added params stay at 4).

Argumentation: The modular architecture already demonstrated the best combined score (0.89) with lower validation/test loss than the seed's flat approach. Adding a lightweight symmetric phase layer targeting qubit pairs symmetric about the center is a natural way to inject additional local nonlinearity in phase space, which especially helps RZ/CRZ-heavy circuits where phase information otherwise gets underused. Placing it right after the RX layer (second rotation axis) and before skip-2 entanglement (mid-range mixing) means the phases get entangled into the ring/skip/diameter structure fully, per the recommendation.
